added_lines: . well played jesus!yes they do. the relationship between religious faith and public life is perplexing. in some societies, even today, there is virtually no difference between the two. in other, more secular societies, any expression of religious conviction is unacceptable in public. it is true of course that there is an appropriate distinction and even separation to be made, as indeed jesus does make today in the gospel. but on at least two issues, there is bound to be some crossover. religious faith informs our values and in society today policies and laws must be grounded, not in a particular faith certainly, but in values nevertheless. prayer lord, we need your wisdom to tell what belongs to god and what belongs to caesar. send your holy spirit into the heart of all believers that we may be true to ourselves and tolerant towards people with whom we disagree. world mission sunday the catholic church celebrates world mission sunday on sunday, 18 october 2026. this year's celebration marks a monumental historic milestone: the 100th anniversary of world mission sunday, which was originally established back in 1926 by pope pius xi. the theme chosen by pope leo xiv for this centenary year is "one in christ, united in mission".1. the story sees a mixture of religion and politics, a potentially explosive combination. jesus does not ask us to avoid politics, but that our involvement in the affairs of the world be informed by the perspective of the reign of god. how does the gospel give you a vision of how your involvement in society should be? 2. pharisees and herodians were not natural allies but a shared dislike of jesus brought them together in an attempt to discredit him. perhaps you experience the same opposition in society today when you profess to being a christian or a catholic. jesus did not get into an argument with them but simply professed his belief in the priority of god in his life. what have you found helpful in bearing witness to the fact that you are still a believing christian or still go to church? 3. jesus recognises that we can be faced with con/f_licting claims for attention. he does not tell us how to solve that dilemma, but challenges us to make sure that our allegiance to god takes priority. when have you been faced with a con/f_lict of loyalties? what helped you to get your priorities right? prayer o god, whose image we bear and whose name we carry, yours is the world and all it contains. recall us to our true allegiance, so that above the power and rulers of this world you alone may claim our fullest loyalty and love. we make our prayer through our lord jesus christ, your son, who lives and reigns with you in the unity of the holy spirit, god for ever and ever. amen.• first reading — isaiah 45:1, 4–6: god calls king cyrus of persia—a pagan ruler who does not even know the lord—by name and uses him to free the exiled israelites. this shows that all earthly powers and political leaders ultimately operate under god's supreme authority. second reading — 1 thessalonians 1:1–5b: st. paul, silvanus, and timothy greet the young christian community in thessalonica, praising their active faith, labor of love, and steadfast hope in jesus christ. gospel — matthew 22:15–21: pharisees and herodians try to trap jesus with a political question about whether it is lawful to pay the census tax to caesar. looking at a coin bearing caesar’s image, jesus gives his famous reply: "repay to caesar what belongs to caesar, and to god what belongs to god". second collection w/e 17th/18th. october propagation of the faith. tablet of 10/10. they may, in fact, have spawned countless new variations on the ancient themes. idolatry “remains a constant temptation to faith” (ccc 2113), precisely because we are made to worship - that is, to declare, profess, and proclaim that god alone is worthy of our praise and adoration - and we will either worship god or something else. if there is no god, then you are a ‘god’ with your ownlaw, your own rules, and, essentially, your own religion. and what do these numerous, autonomous little gods do? they use, they abuse, they lie, they indulge, they corrupt, and they destroy. this deviant dynamic is captured well in lumen fidei : “once man has lost the fundamental orientation which unifies his existence, he breaks down into the multiplici ty of his desires; in refusing to await the time of promise, his life-story disintegrates into a myriad of unconnected instants. idolatry, then, is always polytheism, an aimless passing from one lord to another.” (par 13). adapted from carl olson’s article titled ‘fidelity or idolatry…’ cwr february, 2019.

all missions and missionaries especially the poorest. in 1922 the society for the propagation of the faith became the primary organisation of the church for supporting the activity of the missionaries. pope pius x1 instituted mission sunday in 1926 and ordered that it be observed in a ll churches and oratories throughout the world as a day of prayer and material support for missionary activity. it was pauline who drew up the basic plan of the society. it is one of prayer, offering up of suffering and making a financial contribution for the spread of the faith. this year the theme chosen by pope leo is "one in christ, united in mission" “holiness and mission are inescapable aspects of the vocation of every baptised person. the commitment to become more holy is clearly linked to that of spreading the message of salvation. every member of the faithful is called to holiness and to mission.” mission is not over. many of the young churches eva ngelised are now producing missionaries to other young churches. many of these young churches are rich in vocations but poor in financial resources. all financial contributions for mission sunday go directly to the missions. it assists missionaries to” make his face shine “before the millions who have never had the opportunity to hear about or see the face of christ. it is the one day in the year that pope leo asks your extra generosity on this day, collections will be taken up throughout the world and used to help support missionaries who bring faith, hope and love to those who are suffering on this day, your from the deacon’s desk this sunday’s gospel giving to god what belongs to god matthew 22:15-21 in this sunday’s gospel, jesus is confronted with a question designed to trap him: should taxes be paid to caesar? his response is both simple and profound: “give back to caesar what belongs to caesar, and to god what belongs to god.” jesus acknowledges our responsibilities as citizens and members of society. we have duties towards the communities in which we live and work. yet he reminds us that there is a deeper loyalty that comes before all others. while coins may bear the image of caesar, each human person bears the image of god. the gospel challenges us to reflect on what belongs to god in our own lives. our time, talents, relationships, compassion, and faith are gifts entrusted to us by the lord. as we fulfil our earthly responsibilities, we are also called to offer ourselves wholeheartedly to god, allowing his values of justice, truth, mercy, and love to shape everything we do. may we live as faithful citizens of the world, while never forgetting that we belong first to god. deacon eric thank you to fr kevin when fr kevin announced in may that he had been appointed by archbishop farrell to a new ministry in wicklow, our church was about to close for essential refurbishment works. as a result, there was little opportunity for parishioners to express their thanks for his seven and a half years of devoted service to our parish. the parish pastoral council recently discussed how we might show our appreciation for fr kevin and agreed to organise a parish collection towards a gift from the community he served so faithfully. special envelopes are available at the back of the church and may be placed in the collection boxes or returned to the parish office. we also hope to welcome fr kevin back to monkstown in the coming weeks for a gathering of parishioners, giving us an opportunity to thank him personally and wish him every blessing in his new ministry. a sad farewell to bruno many of you will remember bruno, fr kevin's bernese mountain dog, who was a familiar sight around the parish. after more than eleven and a half years as fr kevin's faithful companion, bruno has sadly died. anyone who has loved and cared for a dog will understand how deep that bond can be. we know that bruno's loss will be keenly felt and we remember fr kevin in our prayers at this sad time. deacon eric rev eric cooney deacon coordinator of parish administration mobile:

sick calls & synodality - a missionary resource: synodality is not an end in itself. it exists so that the church may proclaim the gospel more effectively and serve the men and women of our time more faithfully. we live in a world marked by profound transformations. wars and violence continue to wound entire peoples. social inequalities are increasing. migration is reshaping the face of our societies. new technologies are changing the way we communicate, learn and even understand ourselves. many people are searching for meaning, hope and authentic relationships. many look to the church for a credible witness to the gospel. faced with these challenges, synodality appears ever more clearly as a missionary resource. it helps the church to listen more attentively to the questions of humanity, to recognize the signs of the times, to value the gifts of all and to discern together the steps to be taken. in this way, the implementation phase becomes a new stage in the reception of the second vatican council and in the missionary renewal of the church within the concrete realities of ecclesial life. this is the responsibility that the holy father, pope leo xiv, encourages us to embrace together: not merely to preserve an inheritance we have received, but to make it bear fruit in the life of the churches and in the mission entrusted to the church in our time. (cardinal mario grech, secretary general of the synod of bishops, at the extraordinary consistory of bishops, convened at the vatican 26-27 june 2026). ' thought for the day: our mission, send me, lord, out into the world that begins at my front door. may my every word flow from your heart and my actions be of love and peace that everything i do or say reflects your great mercy to all. help me witness to your truth no less in my silence than in my words and show me, lord, the way i should go. help me to see that my solemn duty to spread your gospel to everyone in the world is second only to their right to hear and respond to it. open my eyes to your presence in others and my ears to recognise your voice especially in the poor and oppressed. amen. twenty- ninth sunday in ordinary time 18th october 2026 world mission sunday blackrock road

world mission sunday – 18th october 2026 world mission sunday, which is celebrated on the 2nd last sunday of october each year, is the one sunday of the year when thee ntire global church comes together in support of mission. it is the holy father’s annual appeal for spiritual and financial support so that the life giving work of overseas mission and missionaries can continue. mission sund ay collections will take place in every single parish where the church is pr esent. it is a moment of universal solidarity when each member of the church family, regardless of location or background, plays their part in supporting each other. all offerings and donations made on world mission sunday become part of the holy father’s universal solidarity fund. this fund is a lifeline for struggling missionaries and the communities they serve across africa, asia and latin america, where over 1,100 mission dioceses a re found. these dioceses are often in remote areas devastated by and natural disasters or where suppressed communities are just opening up to the life-saving message of jesus christ. as these dioce ses form and grow, so do their needs. the mission sunday collection offers young dioceses the financial and spiritual assistance they need to hel p their men, women and children survive and thrive. the needs of overseas dioceses vary greatly. these needs can include the purchase of a motorbike so a priest can celebrate mass in remote villages, or the building of a church so that people can gath er and celebrate in safety. in essence, mission sunday: provides church-centred infrastructure by helping c ommunities build churches, schools and clinics; prepares future leaders and carers of the church by supporting the training of sisters, priests, religious brothers and catechists; supports missionary programmes that protect and care for children’s well-being by offering safe shelter, healthcare, educ ation and hope for the future. no. 8. vol 28. twenty ninth sunday of ordinary time 18th october 2026

(our boxes will go to a collection centre in cork city or county for eastern europe & africa) . the boxes are then sealed, sent by truck or container and will only be opened again by the receiving child. boxes are given to children based on need, regardless of religion, race or politics. we are motivated to help others based on the beliefs of christian tradition, which are compassion, social justice and dignity of all people. if you would like to participate in this project contact mary at the a. centre (parish ofïce) at

family of parishes newsletter our lady crowned church st joseph’s church & holy family church world mission sunday 18th october 2026 29th sunday in ordinary time ~ year a gospel reflection in the image of god … today jesus meets the pharisees who question him, essentially to catch himout. however, jesus rises to their challenge placing himself above the controversy they are creating. he acknowledges that taxes must be paid, by law. he then reminds them that each person carries another image with them, the image of god, in whose likeness they are made. each of us is called to abide by the laws of the state but also to put first in our minds that we owe our existence to god. this statement makes a clear distinction between the political and religious spheres of life. so, on this mission sunday we are reminded in the gospel of our own responsibility for the mission of christ: to speak of god and to bear witness to him to all whom we encounter. every one of us, by baptism, is called to be a living presence in society, inspiring it with the gospel and with the lifeblood of the holy spirit. it is a question of committing ourselves with humility and courage, making our own contribution to the building of god’s kingdom in our time and place. are you ready to answer the call to mission in this community? family of parishes clergy team moderator & co-pp: fr charles kiely our lady crowned church, upper mayfield, cork. telephone:

world mission sunday – pray for missionaries the 100th world mission sunday message by pope leo xiv. reflecting on a century of global evangelization since the day of remembrance’ was established by pope pius xi, in 1926 the pope emphasizes that every baptized christian shares a universal missionary call rooted in spiritual unity and love rather than isolated efforts. he urges all parishes to actively participate through prayer and financial support for today’s collection. christians who experience the joy of the gospel are asked to share it with poorer struggling churches i n different parts of the world. this can be done firstly, by praying for the missionaries who go out from a local church to bring the message of the gospel to others – and secondly, by financially supporting the work of mission in these places. contributions are used to build simple mission churches, to educate and nurture future leaders of the church. the mission sunday gift is also used for building health facilities for children and adults as well as for providing emergency aid in times of war or natural disaster or to assist missionaries in their efforts to care for refugees. on mission sunday, in a special way, we celebrate the work of about thirteen hundred irish born missionaries and all missionaries throughout the world. we thank god for them; and for all who support them in our own country. priests of the area: fr. tomás walsh, sma. pp (

reflection on today’s gospel: what does the term ‘apostle’ mean? it is someone who is sent. jesus himself was sent by the father to reveal god to the world and to redeem humanity. jesus chose twelve of his followers and they acted as his core group of collaborators. their closeness to jesus over the time of his public ministry was a preparation for their mission in life. just as jesus had been sent by the father, jesus in turn sent out his twelve disciples to make him known, initially to the jews and eventually to the whole world. in today’s gospel he tells them: ‘and as you go, proclaim that the kingdom of heaven is close at hand’ (matthew 10:7). later in that gospel we read t he great commission, jesus’ final sending out of his apost les: all authority in heaven and on earth has been given to me. go therefore and make disciples of all nations, baptizing them in the name of the father and of the son and of the holy spirit, and teaching them to obey everything that i have commanded you. and remember, i am with you always, to the end of the age(mt 28:18-20) this commission is now the responsibility of the whole church , not just the successors of the apostles. pope francis proposed this extension of the apostolic mission to all christians as synodality. pope leo has continued this emphasis on synodality from the beginning of his papacy. what is synodality?

family of parishes newsletter our lady crowned church st joseph’s church & holy family church gospel reflection: be persistent… and patient… our gospel today is about persistence… just as the widow in the story pesters the judge until he delivers a just decision we too are called to be persistent. persistence in prayer demonstrates that we are not afraid to show our dependence on god even though all around us society says we need be self-sufficient, to look after ourselves. to keep praying is equally looking after ourselves but also the needs of those around us and the needs of our world. the widow in the story is concerned about the delay in getting a response, however we must not only must persevere in prayer we must be patient, awaiting god’s time for an answer and accepting the answer even though it may not be one we wanted! god will always give the right answer to our prayers, even if in the immediate moment it may not seem that way. take time to reflect on what have been the fruits of your own persistent prayer? when you have patiently waited for god’s time and response… parish clergy contact details moderator & co-pp: fr charles kiely our lady crowned church, upper mayfield, cork. telephone:
